The **water** package does not estimate surface reflectance for Landsat 8 and 9. Instead, it uses the products that USGS computes for every scene: [Collection 2 Level-2](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-collection-2-level-2-science-products) surface reflectance (SR) and surface temperature (ST). With them, METRIC can run without the raw digital numbers (DN). This vignette uses a small crop of a Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 scene (path 232, row 83, 9 February 2016, near Mendoza, Argentina) included in **water**. Landsat 9 products have the same structure and are handled the same way.

## Getting Collection 2 Level-2 data

Download the scene from [EarthExplorer](https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov/), dataset "Landsat 8-9 OLI/TIRS C2 L2". The package repository also has two step-by-step guides (in Spanish) to search and download the scenes for an area and a date range, from the [USGS M2M API](https://github.com/midraed/water/blob/master/vignettes/Landsat_download_USGS.qmd) or from [Microsoft Planetary Computer](https://github.com/midraed/water/blob/master/vignettes/Landsat_download_Planetarycomputer.qmd). Among other files, the scene folder contains:

- `*_SR_B2.TIF` to `*_SR_B7.TIF`: surface reflectance (blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1 and SWIR2),
- `*_ST_B10.TIF`: surface temperature,
- `*_QA_PIXEL.TIF`: quality band, with the cloud mask,
- `*_MTL.txt`: metadata, with the acquisition date and time.

A full scene is almost 1 GB, so crop an area of interest when loading it, e.g. `loadImageSR(path = scene_folder, aoi = createAoi(topleft = c(500000, -3644000), bottomright = c(526000, -3660000), EPSG = 32619))`.

## Loading the data

`loadImageSR()` reads the SR bands, rescales them to reflectance (DN * 0.0000275 - 0.2) and names them B, G, R, NIR, SWIR1 and SWIR2. It also adds the surface temperature as the last layer, `Band_10`, in Kelvin (DN * 0.00341802 + 149):

```{r, message=FALSE, fig.width = 7}
library(water)
scene_folder <- system.file("extdata", "L8_C2", package = "water")
image.SR <- loadImageSR(path = scene_folder)
plot(image.SR)
```

Clouds and cloud shadows must be masked before running METRIC, otherwise they can be selected as cold anchor pixels. `cfmask()` reads the `QA_PIXEL` band and masks fill, dilated cloud, cirrus, cloud and cloud shadow pixels in all layers, including the surface temperature. By default it also masks a 60 m buffer around clouds and shadows:

```{r}
image.SR <- cfmask(path = scene_folder, image = image.SR)
```

## Weather station data

The weather station data are in `INTA.csv`. With the MTL file, `read.WSdata()` also interpolates the weather conditions at the time of the satellite overpass. The overpass time in the MTL file is UTC and the station clock uses Argentina time, so we set `tz`:

```{r}
csvfile <- system.file("extdata", "INTA.csv", package = "water")
MTLfile <- list.files(scene_folder, pattern = "MTL.txt$", full.names = TRUE)
WeatherStation <- read.WSdata(WSdata = csvfile, datetime.format = "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M",
                              columns = c("date" = 1, "time" = 1, "radiation" = 5,
                                          "wind" = 6, "RH" = 3, "temp" = 2, "rain" = 4),
                              lat = -33.00513, long = -68.86469, elev = 927, height = 2,
                              tz = "America/Argentina/Mendoza", MTL = MTLfile)
print(WeatherStation)
```

## Energy balance

With `surf.temp`, `METRIC.EB()` uses the Level-2 surface temperature instead of estimating it from the thermal band. The satellite is detected from the MTL file (`sat = "auto"`), and `alb.coeff = "Olmedo"` uses albedo coefficients for the Landsat 8 and 9 bands:

```{r, fig.width = 7}
Energy.Balance <- METRIC.EB(image.SR = image.SR, surf.temp = image.SR$Band_10,
                            WeatherStation = WeatherStation, MTL = MTLfile,
                            alb.coeff = "Olmedo", n = 5, Z.om.ws = 0.03)
plot(Energy.Balance)
```

Without `image.DN`, `METRIC.EB()` computes the leaf area index and selects the anchor pixels from the surface reflectance. The LAI equations of METRIC were described for top-of-atmosphere reflectance, so the results can differ from a run that also uses the Level-1 data (see the last section).

## Daily evapotranspiration

Finally, the daily evapotranspiration is estimated with the daily reference ET of the weather station:

```{r, fig.width = 5}
ET_WS <- dailyET(WeatherStation = WeatherStation, MTL = MTLfile)
ET.24 <- ET24h(Rn = Energy.Balance$EB$NetRadiation, G = Energy.Balance$EB$SoilHeat,
               H = Energy.Balance$EB$SensibleHeat,
               Ts = Energy.Balance$EB$surfaceTemperature,
               WeatherStation = WeatherStation, ETr.daily = ET_WS)
```

## Using Level-1 digital numbers

If the Level-1 product of the same scene is also available (dataset "Landsat 8-9 OLI/TIRS C2 L1" in EarthExplorer), it can be loaded with `loadImage()` and passed as `image.DN`. `METRIC.EB()` then uses the top-of-atmosphere reflectance for the leaf area index and the anchor pixels and, without `surf.temp`, estimates the surface temperature from the thermal bands: `LST.method = "SW"` uses the split window method with bands 10 and 11. The Level-1 example files included in **water** are from the same scene, with the older (pre-Collection) file names:

```{r, fig.width = 7}
image.DN <- loadImage(path = system.file("extdata", package = "water"), sat = "L8")
MTL.L1 <- system.file("extdata", "LC82320832016040LGN00_MTL.txt", package = "water")
Energy.Balance.DN <- METRIC.EB(image.DN = image.DN, image.SR = image.SR,
                               WeatherStation = WeatherStation, MTL = MTL.L1,
                               sat = "L8", alb.coeff = "Olmedo", LST.method = "SW",
                               n = 5, Z.om.ws = 0.03)
plot(Energy.Balance.DN)
```
